meta.title: Who really said "If you've been in the game 30 minutes and you don't know who the patsy is, you're the patsy"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Buffett really did write this line — in his Chairman's Letter dated 29 Feb 1988. But he called it a poker saying, and it was already in print in 1979.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'If you've been in the game 30 minutes and you don't know who the patsy is, you're the patsy'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified in Buffett's 1987 Chairman's Letter — but he introduced it as a poker proverb, and Quote Investigator traces the saying back to 1979.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: b. 1930 · American investor; longtime chairman of Berkshire Hathaway
answer.sourceLine: Buffett wrote this exact sentence in Berkshire Hathaway’s Chairman’s Letter dated 29 February 1988 ↗, closing his retelling of Ben Graham’s “Mr. Market” parable. But he introduced it with “As they say in poker” — and Quote Investigator ↗ finds the proverb already in print in 1979, so this is the phrasing Buffett published rather than a saying he invented.
answer.confidenceText: Verified against the primary source — though Buffett presented the line as a poker saying, not as his own coinage.

source.heading: The primary source

docMeta.dd: Warren E. Buffett, Chairman of the Board, Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
Marketable Securities — Permanent Holdings, in the “Mr. Market” discussion

source.excerpt: Indeed, if you aren’t certain that you understand and can value your business far better than Mr. Market, you don’t belong in the game. As they say in poker, ‘If you’ve been in the game 30 minutes and you don’t know who the patsy is, you’re the patsy.’
trail: 1979 — the earliest currently known appearances. The Aggressive Conservative Investor by Martin J. Whitman and Martin Shubik prints it as a chapter epigraph credited to a “POKER PROVERB” (ADS-L citation ↗); Quote Investigator ↗ logs three further 1979 instances and notes earlier examples are likely to exist.
29 February 1988 — Buffett publishes the familiar wording in the Chairman’s Letter for 1987 ↗, expressly attributing it to poker rather than to himself.

April 1988 — Quote Investigator ↗ documents a long excerpt of the letter running in the New York Times on 5 April 1988, and the saying being circulated again as a freestanding quotation on 10 April 1988.
Today — Wikiquote ↗ lists it among Buffett’s sourced letters-to-shareholders quotations, cited to the 1987 letter; loose variants that drop poker entirely now circulate alongside it.
source.excerptNote: Buffett’s own four-word framing — “As they say in poker” — is the tell: he presents the line as received wisdom, and italicises you’re for the turn of the knife.

author.name: Warren Buffett
author.heading: Who was writing
author.metaLine: b. 1930 · American investor & chairman of Berkshire Hathaway
author.bio: Warren Edward Buffett was born in Omaha, Nebraska on 30 August 1930 and built Berkshire Hathaway into one of the world’s largest conglomerates, leading it from 1970 onward and stepping down as chief executive in 2026 while remaining chairman. He is the most-quoted living exponent of value investing, the discipline he learned from Benjamin Graham. His annual shareholder letters — plain-spoken, joke-studded, and published free on Berkshire’s own website — are the source of a large share of the aphorisms the internet credits to him, which is precisely why so many uncredited ones get pinned on him too.

copyAttribution: "If you've been in the game 30 minutes and you don't know who the patsy is, you're the patsy." — Warren Buffett, Chairman's Letter — 1987, Berkshire Hathaway Inc., dated 29 February 1988. Buffett introduced the line as a poker saying ("As they say in poker"); Quote Investigator documents the proverb already in print in 1979 and finds no known coiner.

misattribution.heading: What gets this wrong
misattribution.intro: The attribution itself is sound — Buffett wrote the sentence. The trap is what people take that to mean: he wrote it inside quotation marks, as something other poker players say.

items.why: Buffett introduced the line with “As they say in poker” in his 1987 Chairman’s Letter ↗, making no claim to have invented it. Quote Investigator ↗ concludes that he “did help to popularize the aphorism about poker, but he did not create it,” and that by 1979 or earlier the expression was being used by investors.

Their 1979 book The Aggressive Conservative Investor carries it as a freestanding epigraph credited only to a “POKER PROVERB”: “If after ten minutes at the poker table you do not know who the patsy is — you are the patsy” (ADS-L citation ↗). They were quoting it too. Quote Investigator calls the 1979 instances the earliest currently known while noting that earlier examples are likely to exist.

A heavily shared version reads “If you’ve been playing poker for half an hour and you still don’t know who the patsy is, you’re the patsy” — as on Goodreads ↗, credited to Buffett with no source given. Buffett’s letter says 30 minutes, not “half an hour”; contains no “still”; and says “in the game,” with poker named only in his lead-in outside the quotation marks.

The saying is often pinned on the poker champion Amarillo Slim. Quote Investigator ↗ records that when Slim used it in 2005 he pointed to Buffett and “a million other fellows” rather than claiming it as his own.

misattribution.truthLine: Buffett genuinely wrote the sentence, in the Chairman’s Letter dated 29 February 1988 ↗ — but he wrote it as a quotation. The proverb behind it was in print by 1979, and Quote Investigator ↗ has identified no one who coined it.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentence is the sting in the tail of Buffett’s most-quoted passage: his retelling of Ben Graham’s “Mr. Market” parable, in which the stock market is an obliging business partner who turns up every day with a new price and takes no offence when you ignore him. Buffett’s point is that Mr. Market is there to serve you, not to instruct you. The line immediately before the poker proverb makes the stakes plain — if you aren’t certain you can value the business better than Mr. Market can, you don’t belong in the game.

It travelled fast. Quote Investigator ↗ documents a long excerpt of the letter appearing in the New York Times on 5 April 1988, and the saying being circulated again as a freestanding quotation on 10 April 1988. Detached from the letter, it lost the four words that mattered most for attribution: “As they say in poker.”
detailsBody: Quote Investigator notes that variants which drop the poker framing altogether are now in circulation — versions about meetings, negotiations, or business generally. Those are further from Buffett’s text again: his sentence names no card game at all inside the quotation marks, because the lead-in (“As they say in poker”) already supplied the setting.

The 1979 book that carries the earliest currently known printed version, The Aggressive Conservative Investor by Martin J. Whitman and Martin Shubik, sets it as a freestanding epigraph and labels it simply POKER PROVERB — an author-free credit that is, so far, the honest one.
context.pull: Buffett put the line in quotation marks. Almost everyone who has repeated it since has taken them off.
